catalog_description: Interviewers assigned to a specific interview, with each person's role on the panel and weight on the consolidated scorecard.
Reusable interview questions tied to competencies, with question type, suggested follow-ups, and scoring rubric.
Structured interviewer feedback against a rubric: per-competency ratings, written notes, and a hire or no-hire recommendation.
Bookable time windows an interviewer has marked available, with allowed interview types, driving self-serve scheduling.
Scheduled assessment events between a candidate and one or more interviewers, with time, location, panel, and outcome.
Recertification records where an owner confirms content is current or flags it stale for remediation or archival.
Derived per-item scores for freshness, quality, accessibility, and ownership coverage of intranet content.
Discovered or registered pieces of intranet content (pages, hubs, libraries, forms) with source, type, owner, and governance status.
Assignments of an accountable owner and backup to a content record, with the review cadence the owner must keep.
Governed content-type definitions (policy, news post, hub, library, form, FAQ) carrying default review cadence, criticality, and retention rule.
Scheduled or ad-hoc inventory count sessions, with location, item scope, assigned counter, status, and per-line variances.
Lot or batch identifiers for inventory, with item, supplier, manufacture and expiry dates, and originating receipt.
Bills of kit for sellable bundles: the parent item plus component items with quantities and an assembly-required flag.
Per-item, per-location replenishment policies: reorder point and quantity, safety stock, lead time, and preferred supplier.
Individually tracked units identified by a unique serial number, with item, current location, status, and warranty start.
Per-item, per-location quantity records (on hand, reserved, in transit, available), maintained automatically from stock movements.
Inventory items with SKU, unit of measure, lot or serial control, ABC class, default cost method, and physical dimensions.
Fine-grained stock locations: warehouse, store, bin, zone, or hub used to track where inventory sits.
Append-only ledger of inventory transactions (receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments). Posted movements are immutable and drive stock balances.
Inter-location transfers of stock, with source, destination, requester, expected arrival, and status from requested to reconciled.
Stock locations (warehouse, store, third-party, hub) with on-hand, reserved, and available-for-allocation balances.
Preserved evidence artifacts attached to an insider-risk case, with chain-of-custody metadata for HR and Legal review.
Investment funds with name, vintage, size, type, general partner, and fee schedule, organizing capital calls and distributions.
Internal investment committee memos per deal, capturing thesis, financials, risks, and the IC vote. Locked at the final vote.
Real-estate assets held for investment return, with acquisition basis, debt structure, current valuation, and net operating income history.
People in the firm's external network: founders, executives, co-investors, advisors, and limited-partner contacts.
Three-way-match outcomes linking invoice, purchase order, and goods receipt, with line-level match status that drives posting or exception handling.
Candidate submissions against a specific requisition, with pipeline stage, status, source, and full evaluation history.
Formal employment offers extended to candidates, with compensation, start date, terms, approval chain, and status.
Syndications of a job posting to external boards, with board name, post and expiry times, cost, and applicant attribution.
Published, candidate-facing versions of a requisition on a career site or job board, one requisition possibly having many postings.
Canonical role definitions in the job catalog: title, family, level, responsibilities, required skills, pay range, and FLSA class. Many positions share one profile.
Approved requests to hire for a specific role, carrying headcount, level, location, hiring manager, recruiter, and status.
Individual postings to the general ledger: a header plus balanced debit and credit lines tagged with account, cost center, and dimensions.
Sequential steps in an experience or customer journey flow, ordered from one node to the next.
Key data elements defined by FSMA-204, each attached to a critical tracking event for food-traceability reporting.
Typed instances stored in the knowledge-graph platform, with their attributes and relationships.
Ontology definitions specific to the knowledge-graph platform: classes, properties, and their structure.
Knowledge-base articles backing self-service portals and agent-assist tools, moving through draft, review, published, and retired.
Authored, versioned knowledge content units that move through draft, published, and archived.
Hierarchical organization of knowledge articles into topics, sections, tags, and search facets.
Curated groupings of articles (product docs, process guides, FAQs, onboarding playbooks) with audience tags and expiration.
Typed instances of ontology classes (graph nodes or RDF individuals) with assertions, relationships, embeddings, and provenance, queried by AI agents and apps.
Logged search events used for analytics, surfacing gaps such as queries that returned no results.
Kubernetes clusters with name, version, control-plane config, network settings, and feature gates.
External labor-market benchmarks used to validate workforce-plan assumptions: availability, prevailing salary, time-to-hire, and supply by role, geography, and level.
Per-cow lactation cycles, with calving and dry-off dates, peak milk yield, 305-day projection, and days in milk.

Registered tables and views in the platform catalog over open table formats, with ownership, tags, classification, and a pointer to the physical layout. The unit lineage, governance, BI, and ML all sit on.
Cross-functional tasks within a launch plan, each assigned to a function and tied to a milestone.
Dated checkpoints inside a launch plan, such as kickoff, content-complete, sales-ready, and general availability.
Working go-to-market plans for a launch, covering scope, milestones, readiness gate, and owners.
User-built applications on the low-code platform, with name, owner, deployment, permissions, and status.
Custom domain objects defined within a low-code app, including schema, fields, references, validation rules, and security model.
Configured external connections (CRM, database, REST API) bound to a low-code app, with schema introspection.
UI screens authored as versioned artifacts within a low-code app, such as pages, screens, or canvases.
Business process definitions inside a low-code app: states, transitions, role-based steps, integrations, and escalations.
Scores per lead or contact combining explicit signals (form fills, demo requests) and implicit fit signals, driving qualified-lead routing.
Badges earned by learners, each with earn date, evidence link, and verification token.
Credentials issued to a worker (internal, vendor, or regulatory), with issue date, expiry, issuing body, and renewal rules. Drives recertification campaigns.
Log of notifications sent to learners: reminders, nudges, completions, and escalations.
Reusable content assets (video, PDF, image, audio) referenced by lessons and modules.
Assignments of a learning path to a learner, tracking overall path progress and completion percentage.
Ordered steps inside a learning path, each pointing to a course, sub-path, or external resource with sequencing rules.
Curated sequences of courses targeting a role, skill, or certification, driving ordered enrollment and progress tracking.
Personalized learning plans composed of multiple paths or courses, often manager-curated or recommended against skill gaps.
Per-learner content suggestions generated from skill gaps and the learner's role profile.
Granular completion events for a course or activity (actor, verb, object, result, timestamp) feeding skill profiles and certifications.
Lessee lease contracts as the accounting subledger record: parties, leased asset, dates, term, options, and payment terms.
Classification decisions for a lease (finance versus operating, single lessee model) with supporting test results, re-tested on modification.
Tracked obligation deadlines on a lease: option-exercise windows, renewal and notice dates, rent reviews, and termination deadlines, with alerting.
Prepared lease-accounting disclosures for a reporting period: discount rate, remaining term, maturity analysis, and lease cost, frozen once filed.
Source documents attached to a lease: the executed contract, amendments, abstracts, and correspondence evidencing the terms.
Lease liabilities measured at the present value of unpaid payments, unwound with interest and remeasured on modification or reassessment.
Changes to a lease and their accounting consequences: scope or consideration changes, remeasurements, rate updates, and impairments, with before-and-after balances.
Period-by-period schedules of lease cash flows, liability amortization, and right-of-use asset amortization driving recognition and disclosure.
Documented legal opinions and consultations, with matter reference, advice narrative, scope, confidence, review date, and privilege classification.
Court-centric tracking for litigated matters: court, case number, judge, calendar dates, opposing counsel, and key documents.
Contracts with counterparties or suppliers, covering type, value, key dates, governing law, and lifecycle from draft to terminated.
Statutory companies, with legal name, registration, jurisdiction, currency, and fiscal calendar. Books are kept per entity and consolidated upward.
Litigation preservation notices, with matter reference, affected record types, custodian scope, and issued and lifting dates, enforced across data systems.
Business-unit requests for legal advice or service, with description, priority, required-by date, and triage outcome. The front door to legal services.
Law-firm matters (cases, transactions, advisory engagements) with client, opposing parties, key dates, responsible attorneys, billing rates, and status.
Individual lessons inside a course module: a video, document, SCORM block, or live activity.
Orders for library materials from a book vendor, with line items, fund allocations, EDI exchange status, and receiving workflow.
Controlled-vocabulary records for names, subjects, organizations, or titles used as headings, supporting consistent retrieval and disambiguation.
Rules defining loan period, renewal limits, fine accrual, and hold behavior for each combination of item type and patron category.
License agreements for electronic resources (databases, ebooks, ejournals), with authorized users, concurrent-user limits, and renewal terms.
Charges against a patron account for overdue, lost, or damaged items, with assessment, payment, and waiver workflow.
Summaries of which copies of a title exist at a given location, including serial coverage statements and shelf-location information.
Patron requests to reserve a title or specific item for later pickup, with queue position, pickup location, and trap status.
Physical or digital copies of a work held by the library, each with its own barcode, location, status, and circulation history.
Circulation transactions recording the loan of an item to a patron, with due date, renewal history, and return status.
Classifications of patrons (student, faculty, staff, public, juvenile) that drive circulation policy and access entitlement.
Registered library members with borrowing privileges, contact information, patron category, and account history.
Patron-owned saved queries or reading lists, optionally configured to alert when new matching items are added to the catalog.
Active subscriptions to periodicals or continuing resources, with issue prediction, check-in records, claim history, and renewal schedule.
Partner libraries or consortium members for resource sharing, with agreement terms, default lending policies, and contact endpoints.
Book or serials vendor relationships managed by the library, with account credentials, EDI settings, claiming defaults, and contacts.
